newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin 96 profit seen up despite charges.
newsitem.headline: Michelin 96 profit seen up despite charges.

text.p: Tyremaker Cie Gnrale des Ets Michelin is expected to report a jump in profit for 1996 on Tuesday despite charges to restructure its Spanish operations and cut 1,445 jobs in France.

A consensus estimate of more than 40 brokers compiled by consultants Jacques Chahine Finance shows a median forecast of 3.4 billion francs of net attributable profit for 1996, compared with 2.8 billion for 1995.
Estimates ranged from just under three billion to four billion francs, Jacques Chahine said.
Michelin will report its results at 0500 GMT on Tuesday and through financial statements in several newspapers.

Analysts expect the results to include a 709 million franc charge taken in the first half of 1996 for a restructuring of its Spanish activities, a smaller charge for the French job cuts announced last month, and a capital gain from the sale of a 2.6 percent stake in PSA Peugeot Citroen in December.
One analyst, whose estimate of 3.3 billion francs was very close to the consensus, said he expected a 250 million franc charge for the job cuts in France.
Michelin's 1995 results included a 72 billion franc exceptional gain.

Last September, when it issued its first-half 1996 results, Michelin did not dispute a consensus forecast for 1996 between three and 3.5 billion francs that had been compiled before the Spanish charge was announced.
The company said in its first-half statement that it expected 1996 results to confirm "the improvement it has been achieving since 1994" due to a major restructuring.

Finance director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere said in September 1996 that lower raw materials prices would show up in the second-half results. He said in late January that the U.S. dollar's gains were also slightly advantageous for the group.

The market will also be watching the evolution of Michelin's debt. Including subordinated debt, it stood at 23.2 billion francs at the end of June, for a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.97. The company recently said an ideal ratio would be between one and 1.3.

It announced the redemption of 3.5 billion francs of convertible bonds in February, the second such operation in the past six months. Analysts said the redemptions would reduce Michelin's debt by around five billion francs and help it reach its debt objectives before the end of 1997.
